title: Normal projective preparation and locality for valuation-curve modifications
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^	imes$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $X$ be a $T$-curve with smooth generic fibre. Its normalization $X^
u	o X$ is a finite $\eta$-modification, $X^
u$ is normal, and $X^
u$ is a $T$-curve with geometrically reduced fibres. More generally, if $g:Y	o X$ is an $\eta$-modification whose source $Y$ is normal, then $g$ factors uniquely through $X^
u$. If $X$ is normal and affine, it is an open subscheme of a normal projective $T$-curve $\overline X$ with geometrically reduced fibres. Here projective means admitting a closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_T$ [def-pc-projective-morphism].
For an $\eta$-modification $f:Y	o X$ between normal $T$-curves with smooth generic fibres, the modification locus (the smallest closed subset off which $f$ is an isomorphism) is a finite set, quasi-finite over $T$ (finite type with finite fibres). Given a closed point $x$ of that locus, with image $s\in T$, the diagram can be studied after replacing $V$ by $V_s$ and shrinking $X$ about $x$ so that $X$ is connected affine and $x$ is its only closed modification point. The restricted modification extends to $\overline X$ by the identity off $X$, giving a normal proper $T$-curve $\overline Y$ with geometrically reduced fibres. Normal intermediate $\eta$-modification diagrams of this extended diagram restrict to the original open. Those intermediate diagrams which are isomorphisms wherever the extended $f$ is an isomorphism spread back from the localization at $s$ to a neighbourhood of $x$ and glue with the unchanged $Y$ elsewhere; the resulting intermediate maps are normal $\eta$-modifications of the original diagram. The curves and maps near $f^{-1}(x)$ are unchanged, and the gluing is an isomorphism off the locus supported over the generalizations of $x$. These assertions also hold for multipointed curves by taking the schematic closures of the generic markings on all intermediate curves. A $T$-curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A geometric fibre is the base change of a fibre to an algebraic closure of its residue field [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; geometrically reduced means all such fibres have no nonzero nilpotents. An $\eta$-modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] which is an isomorphism over the generic fibre and over schematically dense open subschemes; schematic density means injectivity of $\mathcal O_Z	o j_*\mathcal O_U$ for the open inclusion. A scheme is normal if every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Its normalization means the scheme obtained by taking the integral closure of its structure sheaf in the product of the function fields of its irreducible components; for an integral scheme this is [def-sc-normalization]. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X	o T$, $D	o T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D	o T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'	o X$, $f_D:D'	o D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z	o j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.
